newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - CD Warehouse CEO sees growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CD Warehouse CEO sees growth.

text.p: At a time when several music retail chains are shutting stores and trying to avoid bankruptcy, CD Warehouse Inc seems to be bucking the trend.
The 120-store chain, whose sales come mostly from used compact discs, plans to add 36 new stores to the chain in 1997 and grow by 20 percent annually for the next five years.

"What's wrong is that music retailers have gone into very large, expensive pieces of real estate...and the margins on new music alone are simply not enough to cover that overhead," said CD Warehouse chief executive officer Jerry Grizzle.

Adverse market conditions, such as sluggish music sales, overcapacity and price wars, have caused retailer Camelot Music Inc to file for bankruptcy last year and Musicland Stores Corp to close over 50 stores since December.
Additionally, industry sources this week said Musicland had asked vendors -- major record labels -- for concessions on payments while it seeks a cash infusion from a third party.
CD Warehouse appears to be bycking the trend because profit margins on used products are higher that on new CDs.
"Our concept is to carry new hits, but most of our sales come from used inventory," said Grizzle.
He said more than 75 percent of sales in CD Warehouse stores come from used product.
New CDs are generally bought for $10-$12 from distributors and sold at $11-$17 apiece, while used CDs are bought for $1-$5 and sold for an average $5.99.
"The average margin on new music is about 20-24 percent, but our stores are seeing margins of 45 percent and up, which allows us to be successful in the music business," he said.
He said CD Warehouse, which went public Jan 22, also keeps overhead low by renting small stores, rather than large and costly mall-based real estate that other music chains rent.
Of the 36 new stores slated for 1997, 24 will be franchised and 12 will be company-owned.
Prior to its IPO, Richardson, Texas-based CD Warehouse owned only one store and the rest were franchised, but it is using proceeds to buy a stake in 36 stores from a franchisee.

Grizzle said going forward, one-third of the CD Warehouse chain will be company-owned stores. "By running our own stores, we can try new concepts and then go to franchisees with some credibility and suggest changes," he said, also noting that at a certain point, the profitability of store exceeds the royalty fees derived from franchisees.

Grizzle said CD Warehouse will continue to penetrate the 26 states it is in, particularly where it only has a single store presence. Grizzle said systemwide sales for all stores were $26 million for 1996, versus $20 million in 1995.
For the nine months ended September 30, the company reported net profit of $140,000 on $3.5 million in revenues.
"I think we're funded properly for the next two years for growth," he said, adding the company has $1.7 million in excess cash from the offering and $2.0 million in bank credit.
CD Warehouse shares fell 1/4 to 5. The initial public offering of 1,000,000 shares was priced at $5 a share.
